FLAIR opens Hong Kong embodied-AI hub with seven technology partners

Eight scenario partners will support training, testing and evaluation in practical environments.

Media OutReach ↗15 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 12

An environment for practical trials

FLAIR, under the Hong Kong Productivity Council, opened the Embodied AI International Applications Hub on October 15. Seven technology partners and eight scenario partners initially cover manufacturing, logistics, retail, inspection and public services.

A testing and improvement loop

The planned process runs from scenario definition and model adaptation through testing, evaluation, feedback and revalidation. Announced measures include accuracy, execution speed, reliability, autonomous completion and safety.

Demonstrations are an initial step

Opening examples included Robotera M7 parcel sorting, Unitree robots and Galbot retail systems. Shared testing could help bridge research and deployment, but the announcement provides no comparative scores or long-term operating results for the hub.
